title: From Microservices to Agents: The Next Evolution of Distributed Systems
gist: Mallika Rao argues distributed systems are moving from decomposing services to decomposing decisions, with agentic systems having runtime-determined control flow, fluid context state and failure that shows up as degraded decision quality. She catalogs emerging patterns, silent failure modes and the observability and bounded-autonomy practices needed.

themes.theme: From service decomposition to decision decomposition

insights.claim: Microservices solved service decomposition while agentic systems decompose decisions, shifting complexity from orchestrating services to orchestrating decisions made at runtime.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Architecture and platform investment will shift toward decision orchestration, evaluation and context management layers.
insights.quote: Distributed systems are evolving from systems that execute workflows to systems that make decisions.

insights.claim: Microservices still rely on deterministic execution with a control flow defined in advance, whereas agentic systems determine tools, data sources and strategies at runtime from context, goals and intermediate outcomes.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Static analysis and conventional tracing assumptions break when the execution path is emergent.
insights.quote: Execution is no longer fully specified at design time; it emerges at runtime based on context, goals, and intermediate outcomes.
insights.locator: Agentic systems differ from traditional services

insights.claim: Agentic systems differ from traditional distributed systems in three dimensions: control flow, state management and failure semantics.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Provides a checklist for evaluating how much existing distributed-systems practice carries over.
insights.quote: Agentic systems differ from traditional distributed systems in three key dimensions: control flow, state management, and failure semantics.
insights.locator: What Makes Agentic Systems Fundamentally Different

insights.claim: Agentic state is an evolving execution context of conversation history, plans, retrieved documents, ranking signals and tool outputs, and as chains lengthen, context management resembles earlier distributed state coordination problems.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Context stores and execution-scoped memory become core infrastructure, echoing consensus and consistency challenges.
insights.quote: context management begins to resemble distributed state coordination problems seen in earlier generations of distributed systems
insights.locator: The state also becomes more fluid

insights.claim: Failure in agentic systems often shows up as degraded decision quality rather than binary success or failure, from incorrect reasoning, poor tool selection or stale context.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Uptime-style SLOs are insufficient; decision quality becomes a first-class reliability metric.
insights.quote: failures often manifest as degraded decision quality

insights.claim: The shift is a natural evolution of distributed systems, and the discipline that made microservices scale (clear boundaries, observability, reliability engineering, platform thinking) will be essential for agents.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Teams with strong platform engineering are better placed to adopt agents safely.
insights.quote: success will depend on combining flexibility with discipline

insights.claim: Separating planning from execution isolates non-deterministic reasoning from deterministic operations such as retrieval, transformation and ranking, improving reliability and traceability.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: A practical pattern for containing LLM unpredictability inside a narrow layer.
insights.quote: separation of planning and execution responsibilities

insights.claim: Systems are moving toward multiple specialized agents for retrieval, ranking, evaluation or orchestration, which improves quality and modularity but adds coordination overhead, variable latency and failure propagation across agents.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Multi-agent designs recreate microservice-style tradeoffs on coordination cost.
insights.quote: specialization of agents

insights.claim: Embedding evaluation directly into execution loops lets systems refine or retry at runtime, but requires latency budgets, iteration limits and confidence thresholds to avoid runaway cycles.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Online evaluation becomes production infrastructure rather than an offline QA step.
insights.quote: integration of evaluation directly into execution loops

insights.claim: Standardized tool abstraction layers decouple agent reasoning from service implementations and give consistent capability discovery, eventually resembling a platform for capabilities.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Whoever owns the capability-discovery layer controls leverage in agent platforms, consistent with MCP-like standards.
insights.quote: tool abstraction layers

insights.claim: Across the patterns, complexity is shifting from service orchestration to decision orchestration.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Engineering effort and tooling spend will follow this shift.
insights.quote: complexity is shifting from service orchestration to decision orchestration

insights.claim: Cascading decision degradation means an early poor decision, such as choosing suboptimal candidate sources, subtly compounds through downstream ranking and evaluation even when infrastructure is healthy.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Early-stage decisions deserve the most evaluation and guardrails.
insights.quote: early incorrect decisions can subtly influence downstream reasoning
insights.locator: One important failure mode is cascading decision degradation

insights.claim: Evaluation-driven retries are driven by subjective quality judgments rather than explicit errors, making them harder to bound and able to increase latency, amplify backend load and create unpredictable execution.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Classical retry budgets do not cover LLM judge loops, so cost and load can blow up.
insights.quote: retry amplification driven by evaluation loops

insights.claim: Silent quality degradation can occur while latency and error rate remain stable, especially in ranking, personalization and recommendation, so detection requires evaluation-aware monitoring rather than infrastructure-centric observability.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Observability vendors will need to ship quality and drift signals for agents.
insights.quote: Infrastructure metrics such as latency and error rate may remain stable, while user-facing quality deteriorates
insights.locator: A third failure mode is silent quality degradation

insights.claim: Each additional coordination step adds latency variability and partial-failure risk, and incremental context updates across agents can cause state drift that appears as reasoning drift rather than data inconsistency.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Longer agent chains compound latency and consistency risk.
insights.quote: state drift and context inconsistency

insights.claim: Beyond latency, throughput and error rate, observability must add decision quality by tracing tool selections, reasoning steps, intermediate outputs and evaluation outcomes.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Decision traces become a new telemetry category and product opportunity.
insights.quote: A new dimension of observability is required: decision quality.

insights.claim: Shifts in tool usage, strategy selection frequency, fallback rates or retry behavior can signal drifting reasoning and often surface problems earlier than engagement or latency metrics.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Distribution of decisions can serve as an early-warning leading indicator.
insights.quote: an early warning mechanism to detect quality degradation before it becomes operationally visible

insights.claim: Reliability depends on bounded autonomy with latency budgets, retry limits and reasoning depth boundaries so flexibility does not cost predictability.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Constraints are a design requirement, not a limitation, for production agents.
insights.quote: bounded autonomy

insights.claim: Hybrid architectures pairing agentic decision-making with deterministic fallback pipelines offer a pragmatic balance between flexibility and reliability.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Production agents will keep rule-based paths for low-confidence cases.
insights.quote: hybrid architectures that combine agentic decision-making with deterministic fallback pipelines

insights.claim: AI capabilities should roll out gradually via experimentation, shadow execution and controlled deployment, and systems should degrade gracefully in decision quality rather than treat failures as binary.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Progressive delivery practices carry over to agent launches.
insights.quote: Progressive rollout strategies are also critical.

insights.claim: The author notes the field is still early and grounds the analysis in experience operating large-scale search, recommendation and serving infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mallika Rao
insights.so_what: Evidence is experiential rather than empirical benchmarks, so claims are directional.
insights.quote: We are still early in this transition.
